What are national values?

Great question! National values are the good behaviours and beliefs that help Nigeria grow strong, peaceful and united. They are the things we hold dear as a country. Examples include honesty, hard work, discipline, respect, patriotism, tolerance, fairness and unity. When citizens practise these values, the country moves forward: people trust one another, work gets done well, and everyone lives in peace. When people ignore them, we see cheating, laziness and quarrels. National values start with each person, including you in Primary 4! Practise honesty and hard work today, and you are already building Nigeria!

What is patriotism?

Well done for asking! Patriotism means love for your country and readiness to serve and defend it. A patriotic Nigerian is proud of Nigeria, respects the national flag, sings the national anthem with respect, and says the national pledge with a full heart. Patriotism is also shown through actions: obeying the laws, keeping our environment clean, paying taxes when we grow up, supporting Nigerian-made goods, and cheering our teams like the Super Eagles. Even reporting people who destroy public property is patriotism. Loving Nigeria means helping to make her better every day. Be proud to be Nigerian!

Why is honesty important?

Lovely question! Honesty means telling the truth, not stealing, not cheating, and keeping your promises. Honesty is important because it builds trust: when you are honest, your parents, teachers and friends can rely on you. An honest pupil does not copy during tests, returns money or items found on the floor, and admits mistakes instead of lying. In the bigger society, honest workers and leaders make the country rich and fair, while dishonest ones spoil things for everybody. People may forget many things about you, but they never forget whether you are honest. Choose honesty always; it is precious!

What does respect mean and how do I show it?

Good question! Respect means honouring other people and treating them well, recognising their worth and their rights. In Nigeria, respect is a treasured value in all our cultures. You show respect by greeting your elders properly, the way your culture teaches, perhaps kneeling, bowing or using respectful words like sir and ma. You show it by listening when others speak, obeying parents and teachers, not insulting or mocking people, and caring for those younger than you. Respect also means valuing people of other religions, languages and tribes. Remember: respect is reciprocal; when you give it, you receive it!

What is tolerance and why do we need it in Nigeria?

Wonderful question! Tolerance means accepting and respecting people who are different from us, in religion, language, tribe or opinion, and living peacefully with them. Nigeria has more than 250 ethnic groups, including Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Fulani, Ijaw, Kanuri, Tiv and many more, with different religions and customs. Without tolerance, these differences could cause quarrels and fighting. With tolerance, our differences become our beauty and strength. You practise tolerance by making friends from other tribes and religions, not mocking anyone's language or beliefs, and settling disagreements with words, not fists. Unity in diversity makes Nigeria great!

What are the national symbols of Nigeria?

Great question! National symbols are special signs that represent Nigeria and remind us of our unity. The national flag is green, white and green: green stands for our rich agriculture and the white stands for peace and unity. The national anthem is the song we sing at important events, and the national pledge is our promise to be faithful, loyal and honest to Nigeria. The coat of arms carries the eagle for strength, two horses for dignity, and the black shield for our fertile soil. Others include the Naira, our currency, and the national passport. Always treat these symbols with respect!

How can a Primary 4 pupil practise national values?

I love this question! You do not need to be an adult to build Nigeria. Practise honesty: do not cheat in tests and return anything you find that is not yours. Practise discipline: obey school rules, be punctual, and finish your homework. Practise respect: greet elders and speak politely to everyone. Practise hard work: do your class duties, sweep when it is your turn, and study seriously. Practise tolerance: play with classmates from every tribe and religion. Practise patriotism: sing the anthem proudly and keep your school and street clean. Small daily actions from millions of children build a great nation!

What happens when citizens do not practise good values?

Very thoughtful question! When citizens abandon good values, the whole country suffers. Dishonesty brings cheating, stealing and corruption, so money meant for roads, hospitals and schools disappears. Laziness and indiscipline mean work is done poorly or not at all. Disrespect and intolerance cause quarrels, fighting and even violence between groups. Lack of patriotism makes people destroy public property, litter everywhere, and refuse to obey laws. Life then becomes harder for everybody, especially children. But the good news is that change starts with each person choosing good values. Be the change, and encourage your friends to join you!
